fixes.explanation: True, friend. The king's men set out along the road to the fords of the Jordan, and the moment they were out, the gate was shut. I think that's a very quick door. Rahab's rooftop plan had good timing, and the men she hid were still safe under the flax (Joshua 2:6).

Dawn and the gate aren't her clock, friend. Rahab says to hide in the hill country for three days until the pursuers have returned. Her timer is the searchers coming back, and no gate gets a vote. I've waited on a lot of things in my day, but I never had a plan this clear.

True. Rahab says the fear of Israel has fallen on them, “…so that all who dwell in the land are melting in fear of you.” Picture a whole city with the same knot in its stomach and nobody willing to admit it. Her words are about everyone in the land, and she says it straight to the spies on her roof.

No treaty here, friend. Rahab says they heard what Israel did to Sihon and Og, “…whom you devoted to destruction.” That news, together with what the LORD did at the Red Sea, left Jericho's hearts melting. It's a heavy part of the story, and it shows why the whole city was afraid.

Yes, family. She asks them to spare her father and mother, her brothers and sisters, and all who belong to them. Think about that. Rahab just risked everything for two strangers, and the first thing she thinks about is the people she loves. I think that tells you a lot about her heart. She also asks for a sure sign, because she wants more than a quick promise.

Ai isn't on her map, friend. Rahab says, “Go to the hill country…” and the reason is simple: so their pursuers will not find them. She doesn't send them to a city, because a city is where the searchers would look. The hills are the hiding spot. I once hid in the back of a drawer for years, so trust me, picking the right hiding place matters.

The gate isn't her marker, friend. Rahab says to hide in the hill country for three days until the pursuers have returned. Her clock is the searchers coming back, not the sun or a door. I like a plan with a built-in timer. Hide, wait, and when the coast is clear, off they go.
